title: Microsoft Teams: start side conversations from the meeting chat
summary: The briefing accurately reports Microsoft's rollout notice and documents the existing meeting chat control without claiming it governs side conversations. Minor corrections should acknowledge the general Teams licence requirement, a conflicting PowerShell reference note, and the compliance checklist's missing table entries.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown because a licence specific to side conversations has not been published.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included. Replace the licensing notes and the opening Cost and licensing sentence with: 'Manage Teams licenses states that, except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in the organisation must have a Teams license before using Teams. No requirement specific to side conversations is published.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/user-access. Apply that same distinction to Scope, the licensing open question and the cost rationale; do not imply that a feature-specific price has been published.

claims.claim: The Meeting chat setting is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting engagement > Meeting chat.
claims.quote:
go to Meetings > Meeting policies.
2. Select the policy you want to edit.
3. Go to the Meeting engagement section.
4. Set Meeting chat to your chosen value

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -MeetingChatEnabledType Disabled turns off meeting chat for users assigned the policy.
claims.quote:
To turn off meeting chat for users with this assigned policy, run the following command:

Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -MeetingChatEnabledType Disabled
claims.fix: Keep the call, which the cited guide prints exactly, but add this qualification to the row note and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamsmeetingpolicy?view=teams-ps: 'The cmdlet reference additionally says that setting MeetingChatEnabledType to Disabled requires LobbyChat to be Disabled during a feature rollout; the meeting-chat guide omits that qualification.' This reports the disagreement between the two Microsoft pages.

claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/using-admin-roles for the sentence about a role that can edit Teams meeting policies. The existing statement about the narrower cited sources not naming a role need not become a claim that Microsoft has not documented one.
